answer: Verifier spot-checks, funded by the reward, make sybil farming unprofitable. Each epoch a panel from a verifiable random function re-grades a small sample, so no farm knows which identities will be read. Each clone adds exposure, not payment. Detection is easy: an answer that retells a familiar fable under new names, offers velvet prose fitted to any prompt, or mirrors a neighbour in flat echo, is flagged, and the penalty falls on the whole cluster. Exposure compounds across epochs, so expected cost outgrows identity count, while an honest agent only pays for writing something specific.
